project: Sector Forge 1.0 — editor controls and export responsiveness update
scope: Regression update from the 7 November round-trip-verified source. Covers dynamic editor randomise/revert behavior, campaign editor controls, save/export coalescing, map/campaign render hot paths, and off-thread export generation.

javascript_syntax.command: node --check applied to all .js and .cjs files

html_local_references.dynamic_worker_asset: export-worker.js exists and is resolved relative to the same-origin document base URI

coverage: faction field Randomise/Revert and Randomise All/Revert All
faction asset, polity, market-good and generic campaign-story editors
boolean checkbox values, individual Revert and Revert All
table cancel does not run the saved callback
native JSON and hidden entity privacy
GM JSON round-trip and compressed URL data preservation
chromium_end_to_end.environment_note: Normal browser navigation to both 127.0.0.1 and localhost was blocked by the Chromium environment policy. Offline-inline mode exercised the application and its synchronous compatibility fallback; it cannot construct the normal same-origin browser worker.

export_worker.execution: Node worker_threads using the exact export-worker.js source

zip_integrity.archive_crc: PASS — unzip -t reported no compressed-data errors
zip_integrity.extracted_test_results: All checks passed from the extracted archive; Chromium suite reported zero uncaught browser JavaScript errors.

limitations: The same-origin browser Worker path was not exercised inside Chromium because this environment blocks local HTTP navigation. The exact worker source was executed on a separate Node worker thread and compared against the live app privacy implementation.
The synchronous export fallback remains available for file:// previews or restricted browsers and can still pause on large sectors.
Performance varies by browser/device and sector size; this does not prove that no further bugs or freezes are possible.
